newsitem.title: NORWAY: Heidrun crude output soon back to normal - Statoil.
newsitem.headline: Heidrun crude output soon back to normal - Statoil.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil ) said on Monday production at the 250,000 barrels per day Heidrun oilfield would be back to normal later in the day.

"We began to start up the platform this morning and we will be back at full production this afternoon or this evening. We will go back to the normal production level of 250,000 bpd," a Statoil spokesman said.
Output was shut in at 0800 GMT last Wednesday after the flare tip fell off the platform.
The spokesman said workers repaired the flare tip and put it back in place but that it was a temporary solution.
"We may have to shift the flare tip again, but for the time being we can produce with the repaired equipment," he said.
The flare tip, a safety measure for releasing pressure in the processing facilities, was picked up be a ship later on Wednesday.
Latest production figures from Statoil showed that Heidrun produced 249,738 barrels of crude last Tuesday.
